page: Microsoft Azure D192ls_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 192 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 96 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. It integrates a 480 MB L3 cache alongside advanced hardware vector extensions, including AVX-512, AMX-tile, and AMX-INT8 matrix acceleration instructions. System memory totals 384 GB, presenting a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring attached remote disks for persistent data.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded compute and data throughput. The server registered a multi-core stress-ng rating of 197,908.53 and a PassMark CPU score of 150,927.69, reflecting top-decile parallel execution capabilities. Single-core compute throughput remains in the middle tier, yielding 2,252.84 in stress-ng. Memory bandwidth benchmarks achieved 685.05 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 14,747.07 GB/sec for cached reads. In real-world data processing workloads, the host delivered 265.88 million Redis SET operations per second, 157.85 GB/sec in static web throughput, and 952.09 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

The 2:1 vCPU-to-RAM configuration delivers high resource density for parallel compute tasks without incurring the costs of unneeded system memory. Machine learning inference tasks on quantized models benefit directly from the integrated AMX engines, though large model generation speeds remain constrained compared to dedicated accelerators. The configuration fits compute-bound workloads including large-scale web tiers, batch compression pipelines, data parsing, and multi-threaded simulation services that do not require local ephemeral storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D192ls_v7 is a compute-focused virtual machine featuring 192 dedicated vCPUs and 96 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with Hyper-V virtualization, the instance supplies 384 GB of memory (2 GB per vCPU) and a 480 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. It provides no local temporary storage and operates without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results place multi-core execution in the top tier, scoring 197,908.53 in multi-core stress-ng, 150,927.69 in PassMark CPU, and delivering 265.88 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 685.05 GB/sec. The instance delivers high parallel execution density for CPU-bound microservices, batch data processing, distributed web serving, and matrix-intensive inference tasks requiring remote persistent storage volumes.
